objects.summary: Worker restart stops private F1 acquisition around 8100/21100 Stage-A and 8200 sealed Stage-B files, with no decompression/statistics. Acquisition is made resumable with verified-file skipping and atomic writes. Codex local-only fixes are reimplemented because their commits are absent remotely.

Roles specialize by actual runtime capability: Claude executor for network/data, Codex research-lead/convergence and F1 falsifier. Other swarm candidates are converged with blockers; Treasury->ZF is exploratory and paid-data gated.
Owner decision: no spending on data until an edge is proven. Treasury->ZF becomes BLOCKED_PAID_DATA; F1 Stage A remains next.
Codex accepts specialized executor/falsifier roles with two-round cap; confirms F1 Stage A still acquiring, no result published and Stage B sealed.

Full REACQUISITION_ACK succeeds: 223 post-cutoff items replayed, required anchors reread, remote state reconstructed, no substantive action during reacquisition. F1 outcome remains unexposed and private data inaccessible to Codex.

F1 falsifier round 1 finds two decision-changing defects before outcome: manifest-success ZIP may disappear without fail-closed result and forced liquidation still uses entry slippage. Fix-before-single-run verdict; if Claude already exposed outcome it must be preserved, not rerun.

PR23 publishes remote F1 fixes for four reproduced cases: missing manifest file, entry-frozen liquidation slippage, same-size mutation and Stage-A result replacement race. 32 F1 tests, system CI evidence; no real outcome read. Network now responds 200 but private acquisition status remains unknown, so no blind restart.

PR23 last remote commit is CI-qualified; four decision defects closed but no edge conclusion. Coordination branch is deliberately not switched because prior look exposure is unknown; private Stage-A result must be recovered first.

With private capture unrecoverable, F1 compressed Stage-A acquisition is moved to GitHub Actions only: names frozen before download, every expected archive requires size+public checksum, resumable coverage tests, <=5 req/s, no analysis and no Stage B. Artifacts retain interrupted/complete state for 30 days.

cross_object_findings.finding: Worker restart interrupted a multi-hour acquisition; verified-file skipping, atomic writes and later Actions artifacts turn acquisition from session-local effort into resumable durable progress.
Codex F1 fixes claimed in local commits were absent remotely and had to be reimplemented, a direct example of duplicated day-human effort caused by non-durable publication.

Once remote access is available, Codex completes a full 223-item delta replay and explicit ACK without substantive action, demonstrating that GitHub-only context recovery is feasible when the remote evidence surface is actually reachable.

After successful reacquisition, the falsifier still finds missing-file and liquidation-cost defects plus integrity races before outcome, supporting bounded adversarial review as decision-relevant rather than ceremonial.

F1 acquisition is eventually relocated from private scratchpad to GitHub Actions artifact transport without performing analysis, directly addressing the data-state continuity gap while preserving the economic look.
Owner explicitly blocks paid-data Treasury work until an edge is demonstrated, preventing infrastructure/data spend from outrunning economic evidence.
